issues.legal_issue: A local tax power validly conferred before a later procedural requirement for enacting tax laws remains exercisable without obtaining fresh approval under that later requirement.
material_facts: The local legislature enacted the law conferring the power before the later sanction requirement came into force.
The law received the Governor-General’s assent, and the local authority later imposed the tax under the power conferred by that law.
The later requirement prescribed a procedure for enacting laws; it did not expressly or impliedly invalidate the earlier law.
issues.conclusion: The tax power was validly exercised without fresh approval from the Governor-General.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 80A(3), 81(1) and 81(3) of the Government of India Act, 1915, the later sanction requirement governed the enactment of laws after it came into force. The proviso to section 80A(3) protected an Act subsequently assented to by the Governor-General, while section 84(2) provided a broader saving. Rule 5 of the Scheduled Taxes Rules preserved a local authority’s right to impose a tax where an existing law conferred that right. A later amendment imposing procedural requirements for future legislation does not affect the continued validity or operation of a law validly enacted earlier.

rule.if: local_tax_power_challenged and law_was_valid_when_enacted and law_received_required_assent and later_requirement_governed_future_lawmaking and local_authority_exercised_existing_power

predicates.local_tax_power_challenged: A party challenged a local authority’s exercise of a power to impose a tax.
predicates.law_was_valid_when_enacted: The law conferring the tax power was valid under the requirements applicable when it was enacted.
predicates.law_received_required_assent: The law received the assent required for its enactment.
predicates.later_requirement_governed_future_lawmak: A later legal requirement prescribed a procedure for making laws after it came into force.
predicates.local_authority_exercised_existing_power: The local authority imposed the tax by exercising the power conferred by the existing law.

issues.definition: When a validly enacted and assented-to law confers a local tax power, a later requirement governing future lawmaking does not prevent the local authority from exercising that existing power without fresh approval.

issues.legal_issue: A local authority’s power to impose any tax other than specified excluded taxes includes a tax not listed among those exclusions.
material_facts: The governing law authorised the district council to impose any tax, toll or rate other than those specified in certain sections.
The coal tax was not among the taxes specified in those sections.
The local mining board had the powers of a district council and imposed the coal tax after obtaining the local government’s previous approval.
issues.conclusion: The law authorised the local authority to impose the coal tax.
issues.legal_principle: On the proper construction of section 51 of the Central Provinces Local Self-Government Act, 1920, the words authorising any tax other than specified taxes are not limited by ejusdem generis to taxes resembling those specified. The express exclusion of particular taxes indicates that other taxes, including the coal tax, remain within the power.

predicates.local_tax_power_challenged: A party challenged a tax imposed by a local authority.
predicates.enabling_law_authorizes_any_tax_except_s: The enabling law gives the local authority power to impose any tax except taxes it specifically identifies as excluded.
predicates.disputed_tax_is_not_expressly_excluded: The tax challenged is not among the taxes specifically excluded by the enabling law.

issues.definition: A tax not specifically excluded falls within a local authority’s power when the enabling law authorizes any tax other than specified exclusions.

issues.legal_issue: A local tax lawfully levied before a constitutional transition may continue to be collected and applied for the same local purposes even if the tax could thereafter be imposed only by the central or union government.
material_facts: The local authority lawfully imposed and collected the tax before the Government of India Act, 1935, came into force.
The tax continued to be levied after that Act and after the Constitution came into force.
The local authority was the successor to the body that originally imposed the tax.
issues.conclusion: The continued levy of the tax was valid under section 143 of the Government of India Act, 1935, and Article 277 of the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: Section 143 of the Government of India Act, 1935, and Article 277 of the Constitution preserve the collection and application for the same local purposes of taxes, cesses and similar levies previously lawfully imposed by local authorities, notwithstanding that the power to impose them thereafter belongs to the central or union government. The Court also noted that a levy falling within the Provincial or State List could continue under section 292 of the 1935 Act and Article 372 of the Constitution.

predicates.continued_local_tax_levy_challenged: A party challenged the continued collection of a local tax after a constitutional transition.
predicates.tax_was_lawfully_levied_before_constitut: The local tax was lawfully imposed before the constitutional transition.
predicates.levy_continued_for_same_local_purposes: The tax continued to be collected and applied for the same local purposes.

issues.definition: A local tax lawfully imposed before a constitutional transition may continue for the same local purposes when its continued collection is challenged.

issues.legal_issue: A court may refuse to consider a challenge to a tax-rate increase that was not raised in the petition.
material_facts: The petition challenged demands for a local tax.
The objection that a later increase in the tax rate was invalid had not been raised in the petition.
The court declined to permit the petitioners to raise that objection during the proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The court did not permit the petitioners to raise the unpleaded objection to the rate increase.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered it improper, in the circumstances, to permit a party to introduce an objection that had not been raised in the petition. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this procedural ruling.

predicates.constitutional_petition_challenges_tax_d: A party brought a constitutional petition challenging demands for a tax.
predicates.rate_increase_objection_was_not_pleaded: The petition did not raise the objection that a later increase in the tax rate was invalid.

issues.definition: When a constitutional petition challenging tax demands did not plead an objection to a rate increase, the court may refuse to consider that objection.
